articles.title: Data center demand drives 66% surge in natural gas power plant costs
articles.summary:
The rapid expansion of data center infrastructure, primarily driven by the compute requirements of generative AI, is exerting significant upward pressure on energy production costs. Recent data indicates that the cost of constructing natural gas power plants has surged by 66% over a two-year period, while construction timelines have extended by 23%. This trend reflects a critical bottleneck in the AI supply chain: the inability of the electrical grid to keep pace with the exponential growth in power demand. As hyperscalers compete for reliable energy sources to maintain uptime and scale operations, the resulting scarcity of materials and labor is inflating capital expenditures. This systemic strain underscores a growing dependency on fossil fuels to bridge the gap until sustainable energy alternatives can be deployed at the necessary scale.
[**TechCrunch AI**](https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/27/data-center-demand-drives-66-surge-in-natural-gas-power-plant-costs/)

articles.title: AI models need more data about biology, and OpenAI is paying to create it
articles.summary:
OpenAI is aggressively pursuing high-quality biological data to enhance the capabilities of its AI models within the life sciences. A critical bottleneck for medical AI is the scarcity of detailed, structured data, as much of the most valuable information—such as regulatory filings, manufacturing strategies, and safety data—is guarded as corporate trade secrets. To circumvent this, strategies are emerging to acquire data from bankrupt biotech firms, where intellectual property and internal records become available during liquidation proceedings. By investing in the creation and acquisition of specialized biological datasets, OpenAI aims to move beyond general-purpose language models toward systems capable of genuine scientific discovery and clinical application. This shift underscores a broader trend where frontier AI labs are transitioning from scraping public web data to securing proprietary, high-fidelity domain-specific information.
[**MIT Technology Review**](https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/09/15/1144129/ai-models-need-more-data-about-biology-and-openai-is-paying-to-create-it/)

articles.title: Sexually Explicit Deepfake Sites Target 100-Plus Politicians in Europe
articles.summary:
An analysis of 160 deepfake websites has revealed a systemic campaign targeting politicians across 22 European countries, with a stark disproportion of victims being women. This trend demonstrates the weaponization of generative AI to create non-consensual sexually explicit imagery, specifically designed to harass and delegitimize female public officials. The scale of this activity indicates a broader effort to suppress democratic participation through gender-based digital violence. This development emphasizes the critical gap in current legal frameworks and the urgent necessity for comprehensive regulation to address AI-driven disinformation and harassment. As the accessibility of deepfake technology increases, the risk to electoral integrity and the personal safety of political figures grows, requiring a coordinated international policy response to establish accountability and protection mechanisms.
[**Wired AI**](https://www.wired.com/story/sexually-explicit-deepfake-sites-target-100-plus-politicians-in-europe/)

articles.title: Meta’s new One subscriptions put a price on social media and AI
articles.summary:
Meta has officially launched "Meta One," a tiered subscription framework designed to monetize its ecosystem by bundling standalone app services with enhanced AI capabilities. Following the introduction of its Muse AI assistant, Meta is now offering global subscription tiers tailored for individual users, content creators, and business entities. This strategic pivot indicates a shift toward a hybrid revenue model, diversifying away from a primary reliance on advertising by introducing direct-to-consumer payments for premium AI access and platform tools. By integrating AI usage limits and specialized features into these bundles, Meta aims to scale its AI deployment while creating predictable recurring revenue streams. This move mirrors broader industry trends where frontier AI providers are transitioning from free beta access to structured, paid tiers to offset the high operational costs of large-scale inference.
[**The Verge AI**](https://www.theverge.com/tech/995453/meta-one-subscriptions-ai)

articles.title: What execs and politicians are saying about slowing down AI development
articles.summary:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has ignited a critical debate on the trajectory of frontier AI development with his essay, "We Must Pace the Frontier." Amodei argues that the current pace of advancement exceeds the capacity of safety frameworks to keep up, advocating for a deliberate slowdown to mitigate catastrophic risks. This position has polarized the industry, drawing responses from other AI executives and political figures. While some support the call for cautious, regulated growth to ensure alignment and safety, others argue that slowing development could cede strategic advantages to geopolitical rivals or stifle innovation. The discourse highlights a growing tension between the competitive drive for AGI and the necessity of establishing robust, enforceable safety standards before capabilities reach a critical threshold.
[**The Verge AI**](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/995141/ai-executives-politicians-safety-regulation-anthropic-dario-amodei)

articles.title: Rapidly scaling online storage to serve over 1 billion ChatGPT users
Cognition helps Devin test its own work with GPT‑6 Astra
articles.summary:
Cognition is integrating OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra into Devin, the AI software engineer, to enhance its autonomous testing capabilities. This integration focuses on closing the loop between code generation and verification, allowing Devin to independently validate its work and provide empirical proof of functionality before handing it off to human developers. By automating the rigorous testing phase, the collaboration aims to significantly reduce the manual code review burden on human engineers, thereby accelerating the software development lifecycle and increasing deployment frequency. This development represents a shift toward self-verifying AI agents, moving beyond simple code completion toward end-to-end software engineering autonomy. The synergy between Astra's reasoning capabilities and Devin's agentic framework marks a critical step in reducing technical debt and improving software reliability in AI-driven workflows.
[**OpenAI Blog**](https://openai.com/index/cognition-devin-testing-with-astra)

articles.title: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking
articles.summary:
Google DeepMind has unveiled Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking, marking a significant evolution in the Gemini ecosystem. The "Live" iteration focuses on reducing latency and enhancing multimodal fluidity, enabling more natural, real-time voice and visual interactions. Simultaneously, the "Extended Thinking" variant introduces a dedicated reasoning phase, allowing the model to deliberate on complex queries before generating a final response. This architectural shift is designed to improve performance in high-reasoning domains such as advanced mathematics, software engineering, and strategic planning. By integrating these capabilities, Google aims to bridge the gap between rapid conversational AI and deep cognitive processing, positioning Gemini as a versatile tool for both immediate utility and complex problem-solving in enterprise and consumer environments.
[**DeepMind Blog**](https://deepmind.google/blog/introducing-gemini-3-8-live-and-3-8-live-extended-thinking/)

articles.title: Introducing WeatherNext 3, our most advanced and accurate global weather AI model
articles.summary:
Google DeepMind has unveiled WeatherNext 3, its latest iteration of AI-driven global weather forecasting. This model represents a significant leap in predictive accuracy and computational efficiency compared to traditional Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) systems. By leveraging advanced machine learning architectures, WeatherNext 3 can generate high-resolution global forecasts in a fraction of the time required by conventional supercomputer-based models, without sacrificing precision. The model is specifically designed to improve the prediction of extreme weather events, providing critical lead time for disaster mitigation and resource allocation. This development underscores the shift toward data-driven meteorological modeling, potentially reducing the operational costs of global weather monitoring while increasing the reliability of long-range forecasts for aviation, agriculture, and emergency management sectors.
[**DeepMind Blog**](https://deepmind.google/blog/introducing-weathernext-3-our-most-advanced-and-accurate-global-weather-ai-model/)

articles.title: Toward Self-Adaptive Physical AI: Can LLM Agents Manage Long-Horizon Physical Tasks?
articles.summary:
This research explores the viability of using Large Language Model (LLM) agents to manage long-horizon physical tasks in a zero-shot capacity, specifically focusing on self-adaptation to environmental shifts. The authors propose a multi-agent framework that synthesizes planning, tool utilization, environmental observation, and verification to eliminate the need for extensive retraining or human intervention. When tested on agricultural management tasks, the LLM-based framework demonstrated performance comparable to traditional Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents under consistent conditions. Crucially, the LLM agents exhibited superior adaptability when faced with shifted environmental variables, such as changing weather patterns, where RL agents typically struggle. This suggests a significant shift toward "Physical AI," where general-purpose reasoning can overcome the data-dependency and rigidity of specialized RL models in dynamic, real-world settings.
[**arXiv AI**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.13436)

articles.title: Driver Behavior Estimation at Signalized Intersections Using a Physics-Constrained Decision-Conditioned Autoregressive Transformer
articles.summary:
This research introduces a sophisticated two-stage modeling framework designed to predict human driver behavior and longitudinal trajectories at signalized intersections, targeting the reduction of red-light violations and harsh braking. The first stage predicts the binary stop-go decision, while the second utilizes a decision-conditioned autoregressive Transformer to generate acceleration trajectories. A critical advancement is the incorporation of physics constraints, such as jerk limits and target-state conditioning, ensuring the output remains realistic and safe. Leveraging a high-precision dataset featuring RTK-corrected GNSS and physiological data, the model achieves significant accuracy with a 0.49m/s² acceleration MAE and 0.62m distance MAE. By estimating future stopping-comfort levels from a single snapshot, this approach provides a scalable foundation for improving the predictability and safety of autonomous driving systems in complex urban environments.

[**arXiv Machine Learning**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16058)

articles.title: Thomson Reuters Announces Pricing of Public Offering of US$1,300,000,000 Notes and Canadian Private Placement of C$1,000,000,000 Notes
articles.summary:
Thomson Reuters has priced a significant debt issuance consisting of a US$1.3 billion public offering of notes and a C$1.0 billion private placement of notes in Canada. This strategic capital raise is designed to optimize the company's balance sheet and provide liquidity for general corporate purposes, which typically include refinancing existing debt, funding operational growth, or supporting strategic acquisitions. By leveraging both US and Canadian markets, the firm is diversifying its funding sources and managing its interest expense across different currencies. This move reflects a disciplined approach to capital management, ensuring the organization maintains sufficient financial flexibility to invest in its digital transformation and AI-driven product evolution while managing its long-term debt profile amidst a volatile global macroeconomic environment.
[**Thomson Reuters**](https://ir.thomsonreuters.com/news-releases/news-release-details/thomson-reuters-announces-pricing-public-offering-us1300000000)

articles.title: Thomson Reuters Reports Second-Quarter 2026 Results
articles.summary:
Thomson Reuters has reported strong financial performance for the second quarter of 2026, characterized by a 9% increase in total company revenues and an 8% rise in organic growth. A key driver of this performance is the "Big 3" segments—including Legal—which saw organic revenue growth of 10%. This growth trajectory suggests a successful execution of the company's strategic pivot toward AI-integrated professional services and data analytics. The results indicate robust demand for high-value information services amidst a volatile global economic environment. For investors, the organic growth in core segments underscores the company's ability to maintain pricing power and expand its market share in specialized professional sectors, positioning it well for sustained long-term scalability and operational efficiency.
[**Reuters Business**](https://ir.thomsonreuters.com/news-releases/news-release-details/thomson-reuters-reports-second-quarter-2026-results)

articles.title: Can the US and China work together on AI risks?
articles.summary:
The geopolitical tension between the United States and China creates a significant paradox in the governance of artificial intelligence. While both nations recognize the potential for existential risks—ranging from autonomous weapons to systemic biological threats—their deep-seated technological rivalry hinders the establishment of a unified safety framework. Washington views AI leadership as a matter of national security, leading to strict export controls on high-end semiconductors, while Beijing seeks strategic self-reliance to avoid dependence on Western technology. This competition complicates the creation of shared standards for AI safety and alignment. For cooperation to be viable, both superpowers must decouple the pursuit of safety benchmarks from broader economic and military competition, ensuring that risk mitigation remains a neutral, non-competitive priority to prevent global catastrophe.
[**Financial Times**](https://www.ft.com/content/83023f2f-0c12-4239-bf27-99d8e378ec5d?syn-25a6b1a6=1)

articles.title: Nvidia and Meta bosses reject efforts to co-ordinate AI slowdown
articles.summary:
Jensen Huang of Nvidia and Mark Zuckerberg of Meta have explicitly distanced themselves from proposals to coordinate a slowdown in artificial intelligence development. This stance signals a significant strategic rift between the infrastructure and hardware providers and frontier labs like OpenAI and Anthropic, which have advocated for collective safety pauses or coordinated guardrails to mitigate existential risks. For Nvidia, any industry-wide deceleration would directly impact the demand for its high-end GPU clusters, while Meta views rapid, open-source deployment as a critical competitive advantage against closed-model ecosystems. This divergence underscores a fundamental tension within the sector: the conflict between cautious, centralized safety governance and an accelerationist approach to AI scaling and deployment.
[**Financial Times**](https://www.ft.com/content/2e20c674-3386-46ad-b07f-5cd8a013f67e?syn-25a6b1a6=1)

articles.title: Medicare is using AI to approve claims. The result has been ‘alarmingly high denial rates.’
articles.summary:
Medicare's implementation of an AI-driven pilot program for claims approval has come under scrutiny following reports of "alarmingly high" denial rates and significant processing delays. A lawsuit has brought to light warnings from a vendor suggesting the system was not sufficiently ready for deployment. This case highlights the critical risks associated with automating high-stakes healthcare decisions without rigorous oversight or validation. The reliance on algorithmic decision-making in public health infrastructure can lead to systemic failures that directly impact patient care and access to necessary medical services. This development underscores the urgent need for transparency and human-in-the-loop safeguards when integrating AI into government-managed healthcare systems to prevent arbitrary denials and ensure regulatory compliance.
[**MarketWatch**](https://www.marketwatch.com/story/medicare-is-using-ai-to-approve-claims-the-result-has-been-alarmingly-high-denial-rates-db87d902?mod=mw_rss_topstories)

articles.title: Two sailors missing after tanker attacked in Strait of Hormuz, Oman says
articles.summary:
The attack on the oil tanker El Gaia in the Strait of Hormuz has resulted in two sailors missing, highlighting the precarious security environment of one of the world's most critical maritime chokepoints. The incident is characterized by conflicting geopolitical narratives: Iranian officials attribute the damage to naval mines, while United States intelligence asserts the vessel was targeted by a missile followed by a drone strike. This discrepancy underscores the ongoing information warfare and strategic tension between Tehran and Washington. From a global economic perspective, such volatility in the Strait of Hormuz threatens the stability of energy supply chains and typically leads to increased maritime insurance premiums. The use of asymmetric weaponry against commercial shipping signals a persistent risk to international trade and necessitates heightened naval vigilance in the region.
[**BBC World News**](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c3n07ydqdzlvo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

articles.title: Ukraine and Russia Say There Is No Energy Truce, Despite Trump’s Claims
articles.summary:
The geopolitical landscape remains volatile as both Ukraine and Russia have formally denied the existence of an "energy truce," contradicting claims made by President Trump. While the Kremlin has expressed a theoretical openness to such an agreement, characterizing it as a "very good idea," Moscow simultaneously downplayed the potential impact of any such deal on global fuel markets. This discrepancy highlights a significant gap between the U.S. administration's diplomatic rhetoric and the operational realities on the ground. For global energy markets, this lack of a formal truce suggests that volatility will persist, as energy infrastructure remains a primary target in the ongoing conflict. The situation underscores the complexities of brokering peace in a high-stakes environment where energy security is leveraged as a strategic weapon.
[**New York Times**](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/15/world/europe/trump-energy-truce-ukraine-russia.html)
